sites.quote: If authentication of the link is desired, an implementation MUST specify the Authentication-Protocol Configuration Option during Link Establishment phase.
MUST This word, or the adjective "required", means that the definition is an absolute requirement of the specification.
sites.reason: Section 1.1 Specification of Requirements is the RFC 2119 keyword glossary; the sentence defines what MUST means and states no CHAP behaviour.

sites.quote: MUST NOT This phrase means that the definition is an absolute prohibition of the specification.
sites.reason: Section 1.1 Specification of Requirements is the RFC 2119 keyword glossary; the sentence defines what MUST NOT means and states no CHAP behaviour.

sites.quote: An implementation which does not include this option MUST be prepared to interoperate with another implementation which does include the option.
The CHAP algorithm requires that the length of the secret MUST be at least 1 octet.
The authenticator MUST transmit a CHAP packet with the Code field set to 1 (Challenge).
Additional Challenge packets MUST be sent until a valid Response packet is received, or an optional retry counter expires.
Whenever a Challenge packet is received, the peer MUST transmit a CHAP packet with the Code field set to 2 (Response).
Based on this comparison, the authenticator MUST send a Success or Failure packet (described below).
Implementation Notes: Because the Success might be lost, the authenticator MUST allow repeated Response packets during the Network-Layer Protocol phase after completing the Authentication phase.

To prevent discovery of alternative Names and Secrets, any Response packets received having the current Challenge Identifier MUST return the same reply Code previously returned for that specific Challenge (the message portion MAY be different).
Any Response packets received during any other phase MUST be silently discarded.
The Identifier field MUST be changed each time a Challenge is sent.
The Response Identifier MUST be copied from the Identifier field of the Challenge which caused the Response.
The Challenge Value MUST be changed each time a Challenge is sent.
If the Value received in a Response is equal to the expected value, then the implementation MUST transmit a CHAP packet with the Code field set to 3 (Success).

If the Value received in a Response is not equal to the expected value, then the implementation MUST transmit a CHAP packet with the Code field set to 4 (Failure), and SHOULD take action to terminate the link.
The Identifier field MUST be copied from the Identifier field of the Response which caused this reply.
It is intended to be human readable, and MUST NOT affect operation of the protocol.
